body:
> I think this is a step in the wrong direction. For mobile devices we need to work towards being more granular with our resource barriers so that vertex workloads can overlap with fragment workloads from previous render passes. For mobile this is extremely important as vertex and fragment work within a render pass does not overlap.

I agree, I think we can do this a bit better by tracking down the specific case.

I had some more conversations about this, and the main difference is that ALL_GRAPHICS actually covers something that regular barriers can't do, which is layout transitions caused by the render pass. This is the one thing you can't even specify at all using bits manually, which is a bit worrying.

But the main problem is the mobile renderer uses a very particular configuration for dealing with these subpasses, which causes layout transitions. I've yet to see if there's a way to work around it by playing with the subpass definitions more, but we could probably just go with this approach _only_ if the render pass is complex and contains layout transitions implied between subpasses.
